slides.title: Outline
items: Why Japan needed a new eligibility system
How the instrument was built (1995 time study, 1996-98 pilots)
Approaches compared: old Japan, RUG-III, professional judgment, Canada
The certification pipeline: 85 items -> care minutes -> 7 levels -> board
Challenges, lessons, critical appraisal, relevance for WP3

cards.title: Social hospitalisation
cards.text: Few nursing homes or home care; seniors stayed in hospital for years

cards.title: Means-tested welfare
cards.text: Tax-based LTC for low-income seniors with little family support; stigma, no provider competition

cards.title: Subjective eligibility
cards.text: Officials judged income and family case by case; criteria varied by area

cards.title: Political pressure
cards.text: Independent seniors admitted to nursing facilities

items.title: Gold Plan, New Gold Plan
items.desc: Tax-based expansion of LTC services; municipalities plan services

items.title: National time study
items.desc: 51 institutions, 2,376 caregivers, 3,800 seniors, ~10 M minutes, 328 activities

items.title: RUG-III considered and dropped
items.desc: Poor fit to Japanese resource use; needed MDS-trained nurses

items.title: Launch, then first revision
items.desc: Beneficiaries 2.0 M -> 3.5 M; 2003 adds dementia indicator

cards.title: Reproducible
cards.text: Any trained investigator gets similar results for the same applicant

cards.title: Questionnaire-only
cards.text: Results based strictly on questionnaire responses

cards.title: One standard unit
cards.text: Need expressed as estimated care minutes per day. Income, assets and family no longer count

slides.title: Challenges and lessons
limitations: Local variation: leaders boast of raising levels; MHLW flags high-disagreement municipalities
Rising demand; institutions ($450-600/month out of pocket) can be cheaper than home
2003 dementia indicator traded for fee cuts -> incentive to label residents demented
Claude: validity = concordance only; 'ideal institution' yardstick; home-care data discarded; insider account
futureWork: Build the right incentives for seniors, families, providers, insurers
Add an item for expected / potential improvement in function
Promote preventive services; reward providers whose clients improve
Keep revising the model empirically (by law every 5 years) using the national data system

slides.title: Relevance for WP3 (Claude's suggestions - for Nontakorn to decide)

cards.title: Extraction test row
cards.text: Clear domains, exclusions, tool, assessor, output, override, revision cycle; reassessment interval NOT reported

cards.title: Carer-context contrast
cards.text: Japan removed family/housing from the algorithm, yet the board re-adds it (rural isolation, violent spouse)

cards.title: Recovery potential
cards.text: Authors call for a 'potential for improvement' item - early version of a TN-iLTC criterion

items.text: Eligibility = physical + mental status only; income, assets, family removed
85 items -> tree-regression care minutes -> 7 levels, assessed by trained lay officials
A professional board reviews every case and agreed with the computer ~70% of the time
Incentive design drove rising institutionalisation; evidence is agreement-based (insider account)
